provenance.paper: Fang, Warnett & Zdun, Architectural Design Decisions for Monitoring Deployed Reinforcement Learning Systems (2026), papers/spaces/Architectural_Design_Decisions_for_Monitoring_Deployed_Reinforcement_Learning_Systems.pdf
provenance.transcription: Decisions from Table 2 and Fig. 2 (p. 8). The paper gives the number of options per decision (Table 2) and names most of them in §4 (pp. 9-12), deferring the full catalog to its replication package [8]; option lists and descriptions come from that catalogue (memos/add-catalogue.md), whose per-decision option counts equal Table 2. Decision links from Fig. 2. Forces are not transcribed (they live in the model view).
provenance.transcribed_by: Claude Code (implementer), 2026-10-03; no system output was open during transcription, but the transcriber had reviewed the DelveDSpace C2 runs of 2026-10-02 earlier in the same session (see README)

decisions.name: Safe Exploration Strategy Selection
decisions.question: How much freedom should the agent explore during deployment?
decisions.description: Addresses safe exploration in production; the decision is not whether to explore but how to bound it.

decisions.name: Production Monitoring Signal Selection
decisions.description: Determines which signals to monitor, establishing the informational foundation on which all subsequent decisions rest.

decisions.name: Automated Response Mechanism Selection
decisions.description: Selects how to respond when issues are detected, coupling detection directly to intervention.

decisions.name: Reward Degradation Test Statistic Selection
decisions.description: Chooses the statistical test used to identify reward degradation from the observed signals.

decisions.name: False Alarm Rate Control Method
decisions.description: Calibrates the false alarm rate (thresholds) of the chosen test.

decisions.name: Reward Hacking Detection Strategy
decisions.description: Selects a strategy to detect reward hacking, where the agent exploits weaknesses in the reward specification, the evaluator or the feedback loop.

decisions.name: Reward Hacking Mitigation Architecture
decisions.description: Selects an architecture to mitigate reward hacking once detected or anticipated.

options.name: Conservative Policy Updates
